title: Solstice Health pilot - data pathways, redaction & retention kickoff
summary: POC kickoff to define success criteria, workload sizing, and data handling constraints for a 6-week pilot. Major topics: PII redaction, prompt storage policy, telemetry/logging, retention windows, encryption/KMS, and benchmarks to validate latency/cost targets.
transcript:
Header: 2026-10-12 14:00 PDT | Duration 62 min | Attendees: Alex, Priya, Daniel (Redwood); Maya, Lars, Rita, Evan (Solstice)

00:00 Alex: Hey everybody thanks for joining, we'll keep this to an hour, quick intros.
00:12 Maya: Hi I'm Maya, head of data at Solstice. We're trying to scope a pilot to evaluate running clinical note summarization without keeping PHI longer than needed.
00:22 Alex: Great, Priya's our SE, she'll drive benchmarks and redaction details.
00:28 Priya: Hey all, quick note, we'll capture benchmarks that mirror your production distribution — token lengths, concurrency, and chunking.
01:05 Lars: Our typical payloads are 1-2k tokens per request, peak bursts of 80 concurrent requests for auto-summarize, avg qps ~10.
01:22 Daniel: Good, that helps. For pilot sizing we usually do a mirrored workload at 10-20% of production to validate latency and cost.
01:40 Maya: Success for us: no PHI persists in logs, under 300ms tail latency for short requests, and cost per 1k tokens under $0.60 equivalent. Also observability on regressions.
02:05 Rita: Security: SOC2 alignment, KMS-backed key rotation, audit logs, and SSO (SAML). Also we need proof that redaction works for dates, names, MRNs.
02:25 Priya: We can run a token-level redaction demo — Redwood supports prompt-level redaction hooks and on-the-fly masking before logging. There are two modes: client-side sanitization and server-side redaction with a redact pipeline.
03:10 Lars: Which mode keeps cost and latency low? Server-side sounds easier but may store raw prompt in transient logs?
03:25 Priya: By default raw prompt is ephemeral. For compliance we can disable prompt retention entirely or store encrypted blobs with KMS and short TTL. There's also a partial-retain mode where only non-sensitive metadata is kept.
03:48 Evan: For the pilot we want zero prompt retention in the hosted flow, but will allow temporary KV caching for short sessions if encrypted. TTL target 7 days max.
04:05 Alex: Noted. Rita, is 7 days acceptable or do you need immediate purging?
04:12 Rita: For clinical PHI our policy is minimal; 24–72 hours preferred, 7 days might be borderline. For pilot 72 hours is acceptable if encrypted and auditable.
04:38 Priya: Ok we'll propose 72 hour default TTL for pilot, encrypted with customer KMS. One caveat: some telemetry for SLO debugging will still need sampling; we can sample only hashes or metadata, not raw content.
05:12 Maya: We also need deterministic redaction testing: provide a corpus of 500 synthetic and 200 real (scrubbed) examples to validate false negatives.
05:30 Daniel: Actionable—we'll set up an eval harness and run redaction FNR/FPR metrics. Priya will own benchmark run.
06:10 Alex: On benchmarks: primary metrics are p50/p95 latency, tokens/sec, cost per 1k tokens, and model quality delta vs baseline. For pilot let's run against the small and medium model variants you expect to use.
06:32 Lars: We currently would try two model flavors: fast-quantized and high-accuracy. Can Redwood host both?
06:45 Priya: Yes, we can route by policy. For the pilot we'll test the quantized 8-bit variant and the fp16 equivalent; we'll also validate fallback behavior under load.
07:10 Maya: Timeline — we'd like results in 3 weeks, then a decision to expand or stop at 6 weeks. Is that feasible?
07:22 Alex: Feasible. Week 0: integration and sample data exchange; Week 1: benchmark runs + redaction validation; Week 2: telemetry + SLA polish; Week 3: executive review.
07:45 Evan: What do you need from us to start?
07:50 Priya: Network access (VPC peering or private endpoint), sample dataset (see above), and a short list of success criteria. Also a contact for KMS/crypto.
08:20 Rita: We will require a diagram of data flow and evidence of audit logs.
08:40 Alex: We'll share a hardened architecture diagram and our audit log sample.
09:00 Daniel: Bench plan: run 3 workload shapes — small (200 concurrent short requests), medium (50 concurrent long ~1.5k tokens), burst (80 concurrent mixed). Each run will be 10–15 minutes to capture steady-state and tail latencies.
09:30 Maya: Are there any gotchas with KV cache and PII?
09:40 Priya: KV cache is only for model context and is purged after session TTL; we can disable cross-session caching. For PII we recommend encrypting KV entries and using per-customer namespaces.
10:05 Lars: If we do private deployment vs hosted, how does data-at-rest change?
10:12 Priya: With Private (VPC/on-prem) you control the storage; Redwood's control plane can be disconnected and local KMS used. For hosted we offer customer KMS integration and encrypted-at-rest with multi-tenant protections.
10:45 Rita: Also need proof of key rotation and HSM-backed keys — we use an internal HSM for anything production-facing.
10:55 Alex: We can provide KMS integration docs and rotation logs example.
11:20 Evan: On observability, we want token-level cost breakdowns per route.
11:30 Daniel: Redwood Console provides token-level cost and per-route dashboards. For pilot we'll enable limited retention.
11:55 Maya: Competitors we evaluated: OpenAI endpoints, VendorX, and self-hosted hugging infra. How does Redwood differentiate on PII handling?
12:10 Priya: We have policy-based redaction, KMS integrations, and explicit no-prompt-retention modes; also workload-aware batching to reduce leak surface.
12:45 Rita: Last question: legal wants a simple statement on what exactly Redwood stores during the pilot.
12:52 Alex: We'll deliver a storage matrix: what's stored, TTL, encryption state.
13:10 Evan: Ok let's recap next steps.
13:20 Alex: Great recap and owners.
13:30 Maya: Thanks all, we'll send the synthetic corpus and confirm the KMS contact.
13:40 Alex: We'll schedule the benchmark kickoff for Monday next week.
14:00 [call ends]
